podcast.body: Following their debut, Tin Machine released a second album, which, like their other works, struggled to maintain momentum and critical favor among Bowie's fanbase. "There was a second album and a live record, and then the band broke up in 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.body: The sophomore album from the band, which generated their biggest hit, "One Shot," reaching number three on the modern rock chart. Despite this, the album commercially underperformed, peaking at an anemic number 126 and failing to establish the band's independent personality. "And in 1992, the group's sophomore album Tin Machine 2 generated the band's biggest hit, one shot which reached number three on the modern rock chart."
